topic: Using std::getline with Character Arrays in Modern C++
explanation: In modern C++, std::getline can be used with character arrays to read input lines efficiently. It reads characters from an input stream into a character array until a delimiter (by default, newline) is encountered or the specified number of characters is read. This approach is useful for handling raw character buffers, especially when working with legacy APIs or performance-critical code, while ensuring safety through specifying buffer sizes to prevent overflows.
syntax: std::basic_istream<charT, traits>& getline(char_type* s, std::streamsize n); // Reads characters into s until delimiter or n-1 characters are read, appending a null terminator. Returns the stream object for chaining.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of std::getline with a character array 'buffer' of size 20. It reads user input from std::cin into 'buffer' until a newline is encountered or 19 characters are read (leaving space for the null terminator). The program then outputs the captured line. This showcases how std::getline can be used in modern C++ to safely read input into raw character buffers, emphasizing buffer size management and stream handling.
